title: Spiral galaxy NGC 253
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 253, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla, Chile
celestial: NGC 253 · constellation Sculptor · about 11 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #71 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: This wide view shows NGC 253, a nearly edge-on spiral galaxy in the constellation Sculptor, captured by the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla Observatory. The galaxy measures 70 000 light-years across and lies about 13 million light-years away.

Seeing a spiral close to edge-on means we look at its disc from the side, so the arms overlap along our line of sight instead of spreading out as a flat pinwheel. That angle hides some of the spiral pattern, but it shows how stars, gas and dust are layered through the thickness of the disc.

The picture was built from data taken through four filters, labeled R, V, H-alpha and OIII. The last two isolate light from hydrogen and from oxygen, elements that glow when gas in a galaxy is energized, so they help pick out the regions where that gas is lit up. The whole field of view spans 30 arcminutes.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (32.87 x 29.79 arcminutes) and distance (11 million light years), the frame spans roughly 105,000 × 95,000 light-years. Its light set out about 11 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: The Wide Field Imager recorded visible light through R, V, hydrogen-alpha and oxygen (OIII) filters. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Long camera exposures gather far more light than the eye can, bringing out faint parts of the galaxy.
